examples.en: For my health, I'm quitting smoking from this year.
My father quit smoking after visiting the hospital.
I will definitely quit smoking next year.

examples.ko: 금연하는 사람이 요즘 많이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More people are quitting smoking these days.

examples.ko: 한 달 동안 금연하고 운동도 시작했어요.
examples.en: I quit smoking for a month and started exercising too.
My cough got better because I quit smoking.

explain: 스스로 담배를 끊을 때 '금연하다'를 쓰고, 말할 때는 '담배를 끊다'도 많이 써요. 장소의 규칙은 '금연 구역'처럼 명사로 말하고, 반대말은 '흡연하다'예요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 '금연하다' 대신 많이 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common spoken alternative to 금연하다.

phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 담배를 참고 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you are currently in the middle of quitting.
phrases.en_equiv: to be in the middle of quitting smoking

phrases.nuance_ko: 담배를 피울 수 없는 장소를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a place where smoking is not allowed.

explain_en: Use 금연하다 when you yourself give up smoking; in speech 담배를 끊다 is also very common. A place's rule is said as a noun, like 금연 구역, and the opposite verb is 흡연하다.

examples.en: I disinfect wounds with medicine.
Yesterday I disinfected the room thoroughly.
They will disinfect the school classrooms tomorrow.
They are disinfecting, so the smell is a bit strong.
Disinfect your hands and go inside.

examples.ko: 컵을 끓는 물에 소독해서 다시 썼어요.
examples.en: I sterilized the cup in boiling water and used it again.

explain: '청소하다'는 더러운 것을 치우는 일이고 '소독하다'는 균을 없애는 일이라서 같이 하는 경우가 많아요. '소독약', '손 소독제'처럼 다른 말과 붙여 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I disinfected the knee I hurt when I fell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다친 곳에 약을 발라 균을 없앨 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when cleaning an injury to kill germs.

phrases.en: There is disinfectant in the drawer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소독할 때 쓰는 약을 말하는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for the medicine used to disinfect.

phrases.en: There is hand sanitizer in front of the shop.
phrases.nuance_en: A product you put on your hands to disinfect.

explain_en: '청소하다' is clearing away dirt and '소독하다' is killing germs, so people often do both together. It combines with other words, as in '소독약' and '손 소독제'.

examples.en: A gentle aroma spread through the room.

examples.ko: 자기 전에 아로마를 맡으면 마음이 편해져요.
examples.en: Smelling an aroma before bed calms my mind.

examples.ko: 아로마는 향이 강해서 조금만 써야 해요.
examples.en: Aromas are strong, so you should use only a little.
This shop also sells aroma candles.
I relaxed my body with aromatherapy at the massage shop.

examples.ko: 아로마도 좋지만 환기도 꼭 해 주세요.
examples.en: Aroma is nice, but please be sure to ventilate too.

explain: '아로마 오일', '아로마 양초'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙어서 식물에서 얻은 향과 관련된 것을 말해요. 일상의 좋은 냄새는 '향기'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I dropped a few drops of aroma oil.
phrases.nuance_en: An oil with a scent taken from plants.

phrases.en: I lit an aroma candle and relaxed.
phrases.nuance_en: A candle that gives off a pleasant scent.

phrases.en: There is an aroma scent in the room.
phrases.nuance_en: The scent that comes from aroma products.

explain_en: It usually sits in front of another word, as in 아로마 오일 or 아로마 양초, for things related to plant-derived scent. An ordinary pleasant smell is called 향기.

examples.en: I got a silver bracelet as a birthday gift.
The bracelet fits my wrist just right.
A name is engraved on the bracelet.

examples.ko: 팔찌는 손목에 차고 반지는 손가락에 껴요.
examples.en: You wear a bracelet on the wrist and a ring on the finger.
I want to buy a bracelet too.
I bought a bracelet and necklace as a set.

explain: 팔찌는 '차다'나 '하다'와 같이 써서 '팔찌를 차다'라고 말해요. 반지는 '끼다'를 써서 동사가 달라요.

phrases.en: I wear a bracelet every day.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 차다 with bracelets. For rings, use 끼다.

phrases.en: I came out wearing a bracelet today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '차다'보다 가볍게, 꾸민다는 느낌으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lighter way to say it, with a sense of accessorizing.

phrases.en: My grandmother gave me a gold bracelet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료 이름을 앞에 붙여 팔찌 종류를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the material before the word to say what kind of bracelet it is.

explain_en: A bracelet goes with 'chada' or 'hada': 'paljjireul chada'. A ring uses 'kkida', so the verb is different.

en: to rest; to take a break

examples.en: On weekends I rest at home.
I took a short break after work.
The doctor told me to rest for a week.
If you are tired, take a short rest and come back.
I listened to music while I rested.

examples.ko: 내일은 아무것도 안 하고 휴식할 거예요.
examples.en: Tomorrow I will do nothing and just rest.

explain: 대화에서는 보통 '쉬다'를 써요. '휴식하다'는 안내문이나 글에서 더 딱딱하게 들려요. 명사 '휴식'은 '휴식을 취하다', '휴식 시간'처럼 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I'm tired, so I rest well at home.
phrases.nuance_en: In conversation, people use 쉬다 much more often than 휴식하다.

phrases.en: I took a short rest during lunch break.
phrases.nuance_ko: '휴식하다'와 뜻은 같고, 명사 '휴식'에 '을 취하다'를 붙여 조금 더 격식 있게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but built on the noun 휴식 and sounds a bit more formal.

phrases.en: I drink coffee during the break.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉬는 시간을 가리키는 말로, 안내문이나 일정표에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to break time; common on notices and schedules.

explain_en: In everyday speech people usually say '쉬다'. '휴식하다' sounds stiffer and fits notices and writing. The noun works in speech too: '휴식을 취하다' (take a rest) and '휴식 시간' (break time).
